correctness.rationale: Every used color class in \(\operatorname{Cr}_n\) must meet both shores in at least \(h=\lfloor n/2\rfloor\) vertices, giving size at least \(2h\) and hence at most two colors for every \(n\ge6\). Explicit parity-dependent two-color constructions meet the local majority threshold. For even order \(n=2r\), equality in the size bound forces \(r\) vertices on each shore and forbids any same-color deleted pair, yielding complementary index sets. For odd order \(n=2r+1\), applying the same shore lower bound to both colors forces each shore count into \(\{r,r+1\}\); a same-color deleted pair forces the \((r+1,r+1)\) case and a second such pair would create a deficient deleted pair in the complementary color. These arguments give exactly the four stated odd types and the closed counts. The verifier independently checks the original neighborhood definition on finite instances.

value.rationale: Crown graphs are a canonical dense bipartite family obtained by one structured perfect-matching deletion. The initiating invariant is explicitly nonmonotone under edge deletion; here the exact crown calculation exhibits a natural infinite phenomenon: for every odd \(n\ge7\), the complete biclique \(K_{n,n}\) has value \(1\) while deleting a perfect matching raises the value to \(2\). The theorem also classifies every optimum and gives parity-sensitive closed counts, so it is more than an existence check or a routine small-parameter increment.
